source.source_authority: The supplied article is the authoritative source for this transformation; no external research was used.

entry_schema.nodes: Concepts, people, organizations, APIs, code elements, platforms, events, source claims, references, distinctions and other entities.
entry_schema.relationships: Directed edges with source, target, relationship type, mechanism, semantic role, source section, scope and provenance.
entry_schema.provenance_policy: Source-derived claims are distinguished from explanatory models; no outside verification is implied.

nodes.label: React Native
nodes.description: Open-source UI application framework combining React's declarative programming model with native platform capabilities.

nodes.label: React
nodes.description: JavaScript UI library whose component model and declarative paradigm are reused by React Native.

nodes.label: JavaScript
nodes.description: Language executed by the React Native JavaScript runtime on the end device.

nodes.label: TypeScript
nodes.description: Commonly used typed language for React Native applications, adding type safety to JavaScript.

nodes.description: Reusable declarative unit used to describe UI and behavior.

nodes.label: JSX

nodes.label: Native views
nodes.description: Platform-native UI elements manipulated by messages from the JavaScript thread.

nodes.label: JavaScript thread
nodes.description: Background process/thread that interprets developer-written JavaScript in the described architecture.

nodes.description: Data representation passed across the described asynchronous bridge.

nodes.label: Asynchronous communication
nodes.description: Communication mode used by the described bridge.

source_claims.claim: React Native is an open-source UI software framework developed by Meta and the community.
The article lists Android, Android TV, iOS, macOS, tvOS, OpenHarmony, Web, Windows, UWP, VR, Vega OS and visionOS among platform targets or application domains.
The infobox identifies the MIT License.
The infobox gives 26 April 2015 as the release date and 0.87.1 dated 26 August 2026 as the stable release.
The implementation section describes JavaScript running in a background process on the end device and communicating with native platforms through serialized data over an asynchronous batched bridge.
The article says React Native does not manipulate the DOM via the Virtual DOM.
React components wrap existing native code and interact with native APIs through React's declarative UI paradigm and JavaScript.
React Native styling syntax resembles CSS, but the article says React Native does not use HTML or CSS.
The article says TypeScript is often used over JavaScript due to increased type safety.
The history connects Facebook's dissatisfaction with its HTML5 mobile experience to an internal UI prototype and React Native's public release.
The article says React Native was already used in production for Facebook's Group App and Ads Manager by the time of the cited technical talk.
The article reports an October 2025 announcement that React, React Native, and JSX would be donated to a React Foundation under the Linux Foundation.
The article says the React Native implementations for Windows and macOS are currently maintained by Microsoft.

semantic_distinctions.distinction: React supplies the component/declarative programming model; React Native applies it to native platform UI and APIs rather than browser DOM UI.
semantic_distinctions.why_it_matters: Prevents treating the native framework as merely React DOM inside a mobile web page.

semantic_distinctions.distinction: The source says React Native does not manipulate the DOM through the Virtual DOM and instead messages native views.
semantic_distinctions.why_it_matters: Clarifies the rendering target and platform boundary.

semantic_distinctions.distinction: The syntax is similar, but the source explicitly says React Native does not use CSS as its stylesheet system.
semantic_distinctions.why_it_matters: Avoids assuming browser CSS support or identical layout behavior.

semantic_distinctions.distinction: The source says React Native does not use HTML; View, Text and Button are framework components mapped to native UI.
semantic_distinctions.why_it_matters: Separates browser document structure from native component composition.

semantic_distinctions.distinction: JavaScript is the runtime language described; TypeScript adds static type annotations and is commonly used for type safety.
semantic_distinctions.why_it_matters: Separates authoring-time type checking from runtime execution.

semantic_distinctions.distinction: Props are component inputs; state is component-owned data updated through setters such as setCount.
semantic_distinctions.why_it_matters: Supports correct data-flow and component design.

semantic_distinctions.distinction: title: string is required; baseNumber?: number is optional in the example interface.
The examples use function components; the source also names React class components in its description of React principles.
semantic_distinctions.why_it_matters: Distinguishes component declaration styles without implying only one is supported.

semantic_distinctions.distinction: The source describes an asynchronous serialized bridge boundary between the JavaScript process and native platform code.
semantic_distinctions.why_it_matters: Makes execution boundaries and communication mechanisms explicit.

semantic_distinctions.distinction: Cross-platform development reuses framework logic while still integrating with target-specific APIs and implementations.
semantic_distinctions.why_it_matters: Prevents assuming every platform has identical features or zero native code.

semantic_distinctions.distinction: Tailwind use is described as possible through plugins rather than as proof that React Native directly uses browser CSS.
semantic_distinctions.why_it_matters: Separates extension capability from native styling semantics.

semantic_distinctions.distinction: The article's platform list and its Microsoft maintenance statement are separate claims; platform presence does not establish identical maintenance status.
semantic_distinctions.why_it_matters: Avoids overreading a platform list as a support-level guarantee.

semantic_distinctions.distinction: 2015 is the initial public release date; 0.87.1 is a later stable version as reported by the source.
semantic_distinctions.why_it_matters: Separates project age from current-version metadata.

semantic_distinctions.distinction: The article describes a serialized asynchronous batched bridge. This graph preserves that description without asserting that every version's internal architecture is identical.
semantic_distinctions.why_it_matters: Prevents historical architecture descriptions from being generalized beyond source scope.

semantic_distinctions.distinction: Claims quoted from the article are marked as source-reported; architectural abstractions and potential trade-offs are labeled as derived explanatory models.
semantic_distinctions.why_it_matters: Maintains provenance and avoids presenting interpretation as citation.

semantic_distinctions.distinction: The source describes the project as open-source and separately lists the MIT License.
semantic_distinctions.why_it_matters: Separates governance/distribution model from a specific license field.

semantic_distinctions.distinction: Platform support and examples of companies using React Native are distinct kinds of evidence.
semantic_distinctions.why_it_matters: A platform target does not prove adoption by every named organization.

semantic_distinctions.distinction: The example uses baseNumber || 0, which falls back for any falsy value; the graph records the exact code rather than rewriting it as a nullish check.
semantic_distinctions.why_it_matters: Preserves example semantics and the source's exact implementation.

misconceptions.misconception: React Native renders the application by manipulating browser DOM nodes through React's Virtual DOM.
misconceptions.correction: The supplied article explicitly contrasts React Native with DOM manipulation and describes messages updating native views.

misconceptions.misconception: React Native directly uses standard browser CSS.
misconceptions.correction: The article says the styling syntax resembles CSS but React Native does not use CSS itself; styles affect native views.

misconceptions.misconception: A React Native screen is an HTML document.
misconceptions.correction: The source says React Native does not use HTML and presents View, Text and Button as framework components.

misconceptions.misconception: Cross-platform means no native platform code or APIs are involved.
misconceptions.correction: The article says React components wrap native code and interact with native APIs.

misconceptions.misconception: Every platform listed has identical support and maintenance.
misconceptions.correction: The source lists many targets and separately identifies Microsoft as maintainer of Windows/macOS implementations; it does not claim equal support across all targets.

misconceptions.misconception: TypeScript replaces JavaScript as the runtime described by the article.
misconceptions.correction: The source describes JavaScript interpretation on device and TypeScript as a commonly used typed authoring option.
Props are component inputs; state is updated by a setter such as setCount.

misconceptions.misconception: baseNumber is required in the TypeScript example.
misconceptions.correction: The question mark marks baseNumber as optional; title has no question mark and is required.

misconceptions.misconception: The article describes the JavaScript/native bridge as synchronous and unbatched.
misconceptions.correction: The source explicitly describes serialized data over an asynchronous and batched bridge.

misconceptions.misconception: The described bridge details necessarily apply identically to every React Native version and platform.
misconceptions.correction: This graph preserves the article's architecture description with a version/scope qualification; it does not assert universal implementation identity.

misconceptions.misconception: React Native is only for Android and iOS.
misconceptions.correction: The supplied article lists additional targets including desktop, TV, web, UWP, Vega OS, OpenHarmony and visionOS.

misconceptions.misconception: React and React Native are identical products.
misconceptions.correction: React provides the component/declarative model, while React Native integrates it with native platform views and APIs.

misconceptions.misconception: Open-source status and MIT license are the same type of fact.
misconceptions.correction: The article states the project is open-source and separately lists MIT as the license.

misconceptions.misconception: Version 0.87.1 was the initial React Native release.
misconceptions.correction: The article gives 2015 as the initial release date and 0.87.1 as a later stable release listed in the infobox.

misconceptions.misconception: Any performance consequence inferred from bridge serialization is a direct measured claim in the article.
misconceptions.correction: The source states serialization, asynchrony and batching; specific performance effects are explanatory hypotheses requiring workload-specific measurement.

misconceptions.misconception: Every organization listed as a user still uses React Native in the same way today.
misconceptions.correction: The article specifically notes Shopify is retiring its use, so adoption statements must preserve their time context.

misconceptions.misconception: The article's 2025 foundation announcement by itself proves every governance or transfer detail is complete.
misconceptions.correction: The supplied text reports an announcement; this graph does not independently verify its implementation status.

misconceptions.misconception: The article's citation warning proves all of its listed references are unreliable.
misconceptions.correction: The notice says some sources may be unreliable, not that every citation is invalid.
